edit.description: the CLI's own stamped `Logger`, handed to `superviseLoop` and to the tick's `Dispatcher` in place of the engine default
the stamped line off a real verb, both the supervisor's and a tick child's
the engine side stays unstamped for an embedder's own `Logger`

summary: Neither `superviseLoop` nor the tick's `Dispatcher` is handed a logger, so every supervisor and tick-child line reaches the operator off unstamped `consoleLogger`

per.section: A log line carries the instant it was written

acceptance: every line the CLI's supervisor and its tick children write to the operator opens with the instant it was written as an ISO-8601 UTC timestamp — the spelling the tick verdict, the claim file and record filenames already use — while `consoleLogger` writes unstamped, so an embedder routing a `Logger` of its own times its lines its own way
tests: a flume loop run stamps every supervisor line with the instant it was written
a flume tick child stamps the lines it writes to the operator
pins: consoleLogger writes the line it was handed unstamped
notes: Operator's ruling. Verified: `src/cli.ts` passes no `log` to `superviseLoop` (`:1688`) or to `new Dispatcher` (`:1098`), so both fall through to `consoleLogger` (`src/log.ts:29`), which is correct and stays (`.claude/rules/engine-boundary.md`, *Surface, not prescription*). Where the stamped logger lives is build's call; the stamp is the CLI's, so it is not `src/log.ts`.
